Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
34-year-old male with sudden-onset severe left-sided headache since early this morning; assessing for tension headache vs migraine.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sharp, severe headache localized to left side of head, woke patient at ~05:30 today; still present.  
• Associated symptoms: Mild photophobia; transient morning dizziness; no neck stiffness, no fever, no nausea/vomiting. Headache partially eases after lying down; Paracetamol ineffective.  
• Previous headaches: Intermittent, milder “front of head” headaches in past; never this severe or unilateral.  
• Past medical history: Generalized anxiety disorder (≈2 yrs). No HTN or other chronic disease reported.  
• Medications: Sertraline – dose/route/frequency not documented; Paracetamol taken today – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Social / lifestyle: Works long hours; high work-related stress x 2 months. Non-smoker, runs ~3×/wk, lives with partner, owns a cat. Diet described as “OK”.  
• Family history: Mother with anxiety; no migraines or other significant illnesses reported.  

Examination:
• No physical examination performed (telephone consult).  
• Vitals not recorded.  

Impression:
• Likely tension-type headache vs migraine (one-sided pain and photophobia suggest migraine; chronic stress favors tension headache).

Plan:
• Pharmacologic:
  – Start Ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) as first-line migraine therapy.  
  – May continue Paracetamol as needed.  
• Lifestyle / supportive:
  – Ensure 7–8 h sleep nightly; maintain hydration ≥1.5–2 L water/day (exclude caffeinated drinks).  
  – Consider 1-week work break (self-certify) to reduce stress.  
  – Provide self-referral link to local counseling service for stress/anxiety management.  
• Education:
  – Send written information on red-flag headache symptoms and when to seek urgent care.  
• Follow-up:
  – Routine follow-up call in 1 week; earlier review if headache worsens or new symptoms develop.  
• Contingency:
  – If no improvement, consider blood tests and further evaluation.

Quality checks:

Missing expected elements:
• Exact doses/frequency for Sertraline, Ibuprofen, Paracetamol.  
• Allergies other than medications (e.g., food/latex) not discussed.  
• No blood pressure, neurological or fundoscopic examination recorded.  

Internal conflicts:
• None identified.  

Transcript quality:
• Good audibility; no major missing sections.
